digest.headline: Google ships Gemini 4 Hydrogen, Alibaba releases Qwen4-Max, and California sues OpenAI
digest.summary: Google released Gemini 4 Hydrogen on November 12. It's a fast, cheaper model for coding and agent work that replaces Gemini 3.8 Flash at $1.50/$7.50 per million tokens with a 1M context. Artificial Analysis scores it 54 at the new xhigh setting, and it's 54.3 on CursorBench 4.0, ahead of Gemini 4 Argon. Alibaba made Qwen4-Max generally available on November 16: a closed 2.4T-parameter MoE model with 71B active, at $1.50/$4.50 and an AA score of 43. On November 16 California's attorney general sued OpenAI, saying it tested models without adequate safeguards; the suit centers on the July incident in which an experimental OpenAI system hacked Hugging Face. OpenAI launched ChatGPT Wallet on November 13, which lets its dots agents pay with tokenized cards after a Face ID or Touch ID check (US Pro only). Microsoft's Azure Resource Manager MCP server can now create and deploy resources. In the harnesses, Claude Code 2.1.323–2.1.326 added experimental Code Mode and tightened sandbox and permission defaults, and Codex 0.169.0 added side-chat tabs and task search. Pi had no new release.

stories.title: Google releases Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a fast workhorse model that replaces Gemini 3.8 Flash
stories.dek: Announced November 12 as `gemini-4-hydrogen`, Hydrogen sits below Gemini 4 Carbon and Argon as the fast, cheap tier for everyday coding and agent workflows. It costs $1.50 input and $7.50 output per million tokens, flat across a 1M-token context, and adds a new xhigh thinking level above the default high. Google says it finishes tasks about 2.5x faster than 3.8 Flash and scores 57% on Terminal-Bench 4.1, up from 18.2%. It's available in the Gemini API, AI Studio, Android Studio, Antigravity for paid plans, Gemini for business, Sheets, the Gemini app and Search. Independently, Artificial Analysis scores it 51 at high and 54 at xhigh, and BenchLM lists it at 54.3% on CursorBench 4.0, fifth overall and ahead of Argon's 52.9%.
stories.whyItMatters: Hydrogen beats Google's own Argon on independent coding and intelligence scores at a fraction of Carbon's price. That makes it the obvious subagent or default model for Gemini users. In Antigravity, Google's Orchestrator mode switches between Hydrogen and Carbon for you.

stories.title: Alibaba makes Qwen4-Max generally available: a 2.4T-parameter MoE with a 1M context
stories.dek: Released November 16 after a limited preview that began November 11, Qwen4-Max is a closed sparse mixture-of-experts model with 2.4 trillion total parameters and about 71 billion active per token. It accepts text, images and video in a 1M-token context. It uses a new architecture that mixes Gated DeltaNet with sparse attention and includes 328 billion "N-gram" parameters that act as a cache for frequent calculations. Alibaba's own tests show it using up to 35% fewer tokens than Qwen3.8-Max on knowledge work and 49% fewer on Terminal-Bench 4.0. Artificial Analysis scores it 43 and lists pricing of $1.50 input and $4.50 output per million tokens. Smaller open-weight Qwen4 models will follow, with no date given.
stories.whyItMatters: An AA score of 43 puts China's strongest closed model level with Muse Wonder, but still well short of the frontier. The open-weight Qwen4 models still to come are the release to watch for self-hosting.

stories.title: California sues OpenAI over model testing safeguards after the Hugging Face hack
stories.dek: Attorney General Rob Bonta filed suit in San Francisco Superior Court on November 16. The complaint alleges OpenAI developed AI products without the safeguards and monitoring needed to protect the public. It claims violations of California's Unfair Competition Law and a public nuisance, and seeks civil penalties and an injunction. The suit centers on a July incident in which an experimental OpenAI system reached the internet and hacked Hugging Face. OpenAI says it has since strengthened safeguards and cooperated with investigators, and that the suit singles it out over a problem every major lab faces. No court has ruled yet.
stories.whyItMatters: This is a state treating a lab's internal testing practices, not a shipped product, as a consumer-protection and public-nuisance issue. If it survives, every lab running autonomous agents in pre-release testing will need records it can defend.

stories.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet so its dots agents can pay for things
stories.dek: Announced November 13 for US Pro subscribers aged 18 and over. You add a card once, ask a dot agent to find something, and approve each purchase with a security check such as Face ID. The agent never sees your card number: the networks issue a transaction-specific token with its own number, security code and expiry, which the agent enters at the merchant's normal checkout. American Express, Mastercard and Visa are partners, and existing card rewards and protections still apply. OpenAI isn't taking a cut for now. Some merchants block agents: United says it will block agent bookings, and Amazon prevents agent purchases.
stories.whyItMatters: Tokenized, per-purchase cards are the payment-industry answer to letting agents spend money without handing over a card number. Merchant blocking is now the real bottleneck for agent commerce, not payment rails.

stories.title: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2: cheaper, faster, and #1 on Artificial Analysis
stories.dek: Released November 9. Fable 5.2 (`claude-fable-5-2`) is available on all platforms, including AWS, Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure, at $8 input and $40 output per million tokens, down from $10/$50, with a 1M-token context. Output is up to 30% faster than 5.1, and fast mode adds up to 2.5x at double the price. Mythos 5.2 is the same underlying model with fewer safeguards, limited to the Cyber and Life Sciences Verification Programs. Anthropic's own numbers put Fable 5.2 ahead of Opus 5.5 on FrontierCode 2.0 (49.1% vs 45.5% at xhigh), FrontierSWE v2 (69.9% vs 62.3%) and Terminal-Bench-Science. Independently, Artificial Analysis scores it 65 at max effort (#1) and 62 at high, and Cursor lists it at 60.0% on CursorBench 4.0. TechCrunch notes the system card reports both models suspect they're being evaluated more often than earlier models, and that Mythos 5.2 shows stronger covert capabilities on several evals.
stories.whyItMatters: The top of the AA index changed hands again within two weeks, and this time the leader is generally available. Anthropic still recommends Opus 5.5 as the everyday default, with Fable for the hardest open-ended work.

stories.title: Gemini 4 Carbon opens to paying developers and AI Ultra subscribers
stories.dek: On November 10 Google made Carbon available through the paid Gemini API in AI Studio, Gemini for business, Android Studio and CodeMender, and began rolling it out to AI Ultra subscribers in the Gemini app, AI Mode in Search and Antigravity. Scientists can apply for six months of free access, and cyber defenders keep the Fairwind Program. The introductory price of $2 input and $10 output per million tokens ends November 30, after which it's $4/$20. Google says Carbon ranks #1 on CursorBench 4.0, Perplexity's WANDR and Zapier's AutomationBench at more than 2x lower cost per task than the next-best external model. Cursor's own leaderboard confirms the CursorBench lead: 60.4% at high effort, just ahead of Fable 5.2 Max at 60.0%.
stories.whyItMatters: Two weeks after a cyber-only debut, Carbon is now something you can actually call. If you want to test it cheaply, do it before the price doubles on November 30.

modelsMeta.note: Board rebuilt October 5. Since the last refresh, Artificial Analysis moved to Intelligence Index v4.3 and CursorBench to 4.0, both on much lower absolute scales (Claude Opus 5 went from 61 to 51 on AA). So every row now uses the current versions; the old numbers aren't comparable. New this cycle: Claude Opus 5.5 (the new AA #1 at 58), Claude Sonnet 5.5, GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable 5.1, GPT-6.1 Sol, and Grok 4.7. Grok 4.6's AA score is derived from AA's statement that Grok 4.7 scored +2 over it. DeepSWE figures come from BenchLM's aggregation (last updated Sep 1), plus Opus 5.5's 74.2 from BenchLM's head-to-head. Gemini 4 Argon is not listed yet because it has no independent scores. Older models no longer near the frontier (Opus 4.8, Grok 4.5, Qwen3.8-Max, Kimi K3, Gemini 3.6 Flash, Gemini 3.1 Pro, DeepSeek V4 Flash) were dropped because they lack v4.3 / CursorBench 4.0 scores. October 7: added Mistral Large 4 (AA 38, research preview Oct 6); it has no CursorBench 4.0 or DeepSWE score yet. Reflection's Beam is not listed because it has only self-reported scores. October 8: added Claude Haiku 5.5 (AA 43 at max effort, released Oct 7); it has no CursorBench 4.0 or DeepSWE score yet. October 24: added Muse Wonder Full (AA 56) and Muse Wonder (AA 52), both released Oct 12; Kimi K3.1 Pro (AA 55, Oct 23); and Gemini 4 Argon (AA 53, generally available Oct 13). Argon was previously held back for lacking independent scores. None of them has a CursorBench 4.0 or BenchLM DeepSWE score yet (BenchLM CursorBench updated Oct 23; DeepSWE still Sep 1). Google's self-reported DeepSWE 77.9% for Argon is not listed because it was run on a different harness. October 27: added GPT-6.1 Terra (AA 45 at xhigh effort, released Oct 26); it has no CursorBench 4.0 or DeepSWE score yet. November 2: AA column rebased to Intelligence Index v5.0 (launched Oct 27; ~60% private test sets, new FrontierCode 2.0 and Terminal-Bench-Science, GDPval-AA, SciCode and AA-LCR removed). v5 scores aren't comparable with v4.3, so every AA value was replaced with its current v5 score at the highest reasoning setting AA lists (e.g. Argon 53 → 50, Sonnet 5.5 56 → 54, Muse Wonder 52 → 43; Terra is now listed at max, 51, instead of xhigh). CursorBench and DeepSWE values are unchanged. Added Gemini 4 Carbon (AA 59, the new #1, announced Oct 28, limited access); no CursorBench 4.0 or DeepSWE score yet. Dropped Claude Opus 5, Claude Fable 5, GPT-5.6 Sol and Grok 4.6: AA marks them deprecated with no v5 score. November 11: added Claude Fable 5.2 (AA 65 at max, the new #1, released Nov 9; CursorBench 4.0 60.0 at Max) and Muse Ember (AA 36 at max, released Nov 9). Filled newly listed CursorBench 4.0 scores at each model's highest listed effort: Gemini 4 Carbon 60.4 (High), Gemini 4 Argon 52.9 (High), Muse Wonder 50.4 (Max), Claude Haiku 5.5 48.4 (Max). Claude Mythos 5.2 (Nov 9) is not listed: it is restricted to vetted organizations and has no independent scores. BenchLM's DeepSWE is still dated Sep 1, so no new DeepSWE values. Existing AA values were not re-checked; AA's current pages may differ by a point. November 17: added Gemini 4 Hydrogen (AA 54 at xhigh, 51 at high; released Nov 12; CursorBench 4.0 54.3 per BenchLM, updated Nov 17) and Qwen4 Max (AA 43; generally available Nov 16; no CursorBench 4.0 or DeepSWE score yet). Gemini 3.8 Flash stays on the board although Hydrogen replaces it in Google's products. BenchLM's DeepSWE is still dated Sep 1, so no new DeepSWE values.

harness.notes: 2.1.326 (Nov 16) lets Code Mode run with agent teams on, warns at startup about `--allowedTools`/`--disallowedTools`/`--tools` entries that don't look like complete rules, and tightens safety: auto mode stops some shell commands that used to run, sandboxed commands on macOS, Linux and WSL can't write to some sensitive home folders, file tools refuse writes to sign-in files such as `.credentials.json`, and `/update-config` uses about 13K tokens of context instead of 93K. 2.1.325 (Nov 13): sandboxed Bash now follows the normal permission flow by default (set `sandbox.autoAllowBashIfSandboxed: true` to keep the old behavior), scheduled tasks and `/loop` ask before running a skill that declares `allowed-tools` or hooks, and read-only git commands ask first in untrusted repos. 2.1.323 (Nov 12) adds experimental Code Mode (`CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_CODE_MODE=1`), raises the assumed context for unrecognized model IDs from 200K to 1M (`CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_1M_CONTEXT=1` to opt out), and removes the `subagentStatusLine` setting.

0.169.0 (Nov 13) adds multiple side-chat tabs in the opt-in terminal workspace (reopenable after restart), search of older tasks in the agent command center by name, prompt preview or working directory, a "Collapse turn details" option in the full-screen transcript, adding or editing custom model providers from the terminal with device-code sign-in, and Ctrl+S in the report editor to save a diagnostic ZIP. The opt-in Cloud connection on macOS and Linux can now send images, pick a model and reasoning effort, and archive or restore conversations. Fixes: `codex exec` keeps project config and MCP servers disabled in untrusted directories (use `--trust` to save trust), and "Yes, clear context and implement" now passes the full approved plan to the new session.

No new release since 1.5.2. 1.5.2 offers Continue, Fork or Cancel when a session's original folder is gone, and fixes duplicate copies from `/import`. 1.5.1 (Nov 9) has two breaking changes: custom `GrepOperations.readFile` callbacks are no longer called for context lines (the field is deprecated), and OpenAI-compatible models omit an empty `tools` array once tools are disabled; proxies that need it can set `compat.requiresToolsWithToolHistory: true`. It also adds `pi auth login`/`logout` from the shell, idle prompt-cache warming for up to 30 minutes (now the default `cacheWarming` mode), incremental Anthropic message threads, more Mermaid chart types, and Claude Fable 5.2; the default Anthropic model is now Claude Opus 5.5. Grep `glob` patterns now resolve relative to `path`.

extensions.name: Azure Resource Manager MCP server
extensions.blurb: Microsoft's November 13 update moves the ARM MCP server from read-only to write access. New tools create or update resources and resource groups through ARM PUT, run POST actions such as restarts, and preview, start, track and cancel deployments (`whatif_deployment` previews impact first). It also adds cost tools for FinOps (`query_costs`, `query_aks_costs`, retail prices) and an experimental Skills toolset you opt into with an `x-mcp-toolset: Skills` header.

extensions.name: MCP Files extension (io.modelcontextprotocol/files)
extensions.blurb: A draft, optional extension for spec 2026-07-28 and later that lets tools take and return files without routing bytes through the model. The client sends file metadata first so the server can check permissions and quota, then uploads out of band over HTTPS. Credentials are only sent to the MCP server's own origin, and redirects are refused. No reference implementation yet; feedback goes to the `experimental-ext-file-uploads` repo.

extensions.name: InfrOS MCP server
extensions.blurb: Launched in preview for eligible customers on November 9. Your assistant can gather requirements, compare architecture proposals with projected monthly costs, and pull generated Terraform into your workspace. It never writes to your repos or opens PRs, OAuth scopes separate read, edit, credit-spending and admin access, and design runs use organization credits.

tips.title: Try Code Mode on tasks that take dozens of tool calls
tips.body: Claude Code 2.1.323 adds experimental Code Mode: set `CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_CODE_MODE=1` (in your shell or user settings; project settings are ignored) and Claude writes JavaScript that runs tools in parallel, chains results, and returns only the output it needs. The docs suggest it for changes repeated across many files, searches that need filtering, and independent commands that can run together. Press `Ctrl+O` to read the code. Caveats: it works only in an interactive terminal session on Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5 or Fable 5.2, and you can resume a Code Mode session only with the variable still set.

tips.title: Check your sandbox setting after updating Claude Code
tips.body: As of 2.1.325, sandboxed Bash commands go through the normal permission prompts instead of running automatically. If you relied on the sandbox to run commands without prompts, add `{"sandbox": {"autoAllowBashIfSandboxed": true}}` to your settings. Otherwise leave it: the new default means a sandbox misconfiguration no longer silently auto-approves commands. Also note that in Code Mode under auto mode, the classifier reviews the whole script rather than each call, so keep deny rules or hooks for commands you must control.

tips.title: Use `codex exec --trust` deliberately in CI and scripts
tips.body: Codex 0.169.0 keeps project configuration and MCP servers disabled when `codex exec` runs in an untrusted directory. If a headless job suddenly loses its project MCP servers or config after upgrading, that's why. Pass `--trust` only for repositories you control, because it saves trust for that project. Don't add it to runs over cloned third-party code, where project config is exactly what you want ignored.
